summary: This memoir describes how an ordinary man born into a poor family of firstgeneration Chinese immigrants in North Malaysia prior to Malaya's independence positively did not bow to fate and worked hard to create a better life for his family. With an engineer's degree from the University of Taiwan, which is not recognized by the Malaysian government, he started his career as a junior engineer and rose to become a division president of a multinational listed company. He bravely stepped out of the comfort zone of his life and worked for the Group for more than a decade in the early days of China's reform and opening up in a traditional Chinese culture that was full of unknowns. At the age of old age, he should have retired and enjoyed his life, but he opened up his second spring of life and stepped into the unfamiliar world of finance to take on another challenge.

title: FORECAST : WHAT PHYSICS, METEOROLOGY AND THE NATURAL SCIENCES CAN TEACH US ABOUT ECONOMICS
author: Buchanan, Mark
summary: In this thoroughly researched and piercingly intelligent book, physicist Mark Buchanan shows how a simple feedback loop can lead to major consequences, the kind predictable by mathematical models but hard for most people to anticipate. From his unique perspective, Buchanan argues that our basic assumptions about economic markets - that they are for the most part stable, with occasional interruptions - are simply wrong. Markets really act more like weather: a brief heat wave can become a massive storm in a matter of a few days, or even hours. Forecast re-imagines the basics of the financial world, with consequences that affect everyone
